result.topic_en: Green's identity (integration by parts of the gradient product of two potentials V, V') applied to show uniqueness of the potential from a mass density k, using boundary behaviour at infinity.
result.transcription:
$\int\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial V'}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial V}{\partial y}\cdot\frac{\partial V'}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial V}{\partial z}\cdot\frac{\partial V'}{\partial z}\right)\partial S=\iint V\left(\frac{\partial V'}{\partial x}\partial y\partial z+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial y}\partial x\partial z+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial z}\partial x\partial y\right)$
$-\int V\left(\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial z^2}\right)\partial S$
$=-\iint V\left\{\frac{\partial V'}{\partial x}\cos(x,p)\cdot\partial s+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial y}\cos(y,p)\partial s+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial z}\cos(z,p)\partial s\right\}-\int V\left(\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial z^2}\right)\partial S$
$=-\int V\left\{\frac{\partial V'}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial y}\cdot\frac{\partial y}{\partial p}+\frac{\partial V'}{\partial z}\cdot\frac{\partial z}{\partial p}\right\}\partial s-\int V\left(\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial z^2}\right)\partial S$
$=-\int V\frac{\partial V'}{\partial p}\partial s-\int V\left(\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial z^2}\right)\partial S$
$=-\int V'\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}\partial s-\int V'\left(\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial z^2}\right)\partial S$
$V=\frac{a}{r}$ ; $V'=\frac{b}{r}$ (für $r=\infty$) {+$\frac{\partial V'}{\partial p}=\frac{b}{rr}$ [?]+} ; $\partial s=rr\,\partial\varphi$ ; $\frac{\partial r}{\partial p}=\cos(r,p)$
$\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V'}{\partial z^2}=\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial z^2}=-4\pi$ [-...-] $k$
$\int\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial V'}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial V}{\partial y}\cdot\frac{\partial V'}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial V}{\partial z}\frac{\partial V'}{\partial z}\right)\partial S=$ [-$\int\frac{ab\,\partial s}{r}\cos(r,p)$ [?]-]
$=-\int_0^{4\pi}\frac{a\varphi\,\partial\varphi}{r}$ [?] $-\int$ [-...-]$4\pi k V\partial S$
$=-\int_0^{4\pi}\frac{ab.\cos(r,p)\,\partial\varphi}{r}-\int 4\pi k V'\partial S$
$\int 4\pi k(V-V')\partial S=0$
